sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: If you could describe how you were feeling about this election in a single word, is there a word that comes to mind?
sentences.zh: 如果让你用一个词来形容你对这次选举的感受，你会想到什么词？

sentences.en: Hopeful.
sentences.zh: 充满希望。

sentences.en: Anxious.
sentences.zh: 焦虑。

sentences.en: Scary.
sentences.zh: 可怕。

sentences.en: Important.
sentences.zh: 重要。

sentences.en: Consequential.
sentences.zh: 影响深远。

sentences.en: Needed.
sentences.zh: 必要。

sentences.en: This whole administration is a shit show.
sentences.zh: 整个政府简直是一场闹剧。

sentences.en: I'm relieved that it's over and I don't have to listen to the advertisements anymore.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴这一切终于结束了，我再也不用听那些竞选广告了。

sentences.en: Optimistic-ish.
sentences.zh: 还算乐观吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Can I ask who you voted for today in the Senate race?
sentences.zh: 能问一下你今天参议院选举投给了谁吗？

sentences.en: Oh, Abdul said.
sentences.zh: 哦，阿卜杜勒说的。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I'm not the biggest Paxton fan, but to me it was kind of the lesser of two evils.
sentences.zh: 我算不上帕克斯顿的头号粉丝，但对我来说，这算是两害相权取其轻吧。

sentences.en: I voted for James Tallarico.
sentences.zh: 我投给了詹姆斯·塔拉里科。

sentences.en: Nothing against Tallarico, but I think voting for him is a vote for Chuck Schumer.
sentences.zh: 我对塔拉里科没什么意见，但我认为投给他就是投给查克·舒默。

sentences.en: I did pretty much go Democratic.
sentences.zh: 我基本上还是投给了民主党。

sentences.en: I don't always do that, but I did do that.
sentences.zh: 我不总是这样，但这次确实是。

sentences.en: I did vote for Mary Potola.
sentences.zh: 我投给了玛丽·波托拉。

sentences.en: I'm voting for Susan Collins.
sentences.zh: 我投给了苏珊·柯林斯。

sentences.en: I have definitely voted for Troy Jackson, of course.
sentences.zh: 我当然投给了特洛伊·杰克逊。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm going to hold my nose and vote for the dope.
sentences.zh: 是的，我打算捏着鼻子投给那个笨蛋。

sentences.en: I'm going to vote for Troy Jackson.
sentences.zh: 我打算投给特洛伊·杰克逊。

sentences.en: The Senate's full of idiots.
sentences.zh: 参议院里全是白痴。

sentences.en: At least he's our idiot.
sentences.zh: 至少他是我们自己的白痴。

sentences.en: After two years of campaigning, more than $11 billion of advertising, and last-minute dramas
sentences.zh: 经过两年的竞选，超过110亿美元的广告投入，以及最后一刻的戏剧性事件，

sentences.en: in Alaska and Michigan, the 2026 midterm election is now in the hands of the American voters.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉斯加和密歇根州，2026年中期选举现在掌握在美国选民手中。

sentences.en: What's the number one issue you're voting on today?
sentences.zh: 你今天投票最关注的首要议题是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, to stop the current regime.
sentences.zh: 哦，为了阻止现任政权。

sentences.en: The stakes are very high because of Trump.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普，这次选举的赌注非常高。

sentences.en: Everything else pales in comparison.
sentences.zh: 其他一切与之相比都显得微不足道。

sentences.en: We want to keep our country American.
sentences.zh: 我们想保持我们国家的美国特色。

sentences.en: We don't want surrealized at all.
sentences.zh: 我们一点也不想让它变得超现实。

sentences.en: The biggest issue on my mind is the economy.
sentences.zh: 我最关心的问题是经济。

sentences.en: Everything just double, triple, I mean, dang, $4 for a bag of chips?
sentences.zh: 所有东西价格都翻倍、翻三倍，天哪，一袋薯片要4美元？

sentences.en: That's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: There's so many issues.
sentences.zh: 有太多问题了。

sentences.en: How can you think of just one?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能只想到一个呢？

sentences.en: I'm worried about everything.
sentences.zh: 我什么都担心。

sentences.en: Today, as the ballot counting begins, my colleague, Chief Political Analyst Nate Cohn,
sentences.zh: 今天，随着计票开始，我的同事，首席政治分析师内特·科恩，

sentences.en: for how to understand tonight's results.
sentences.zh: 将教我们如何解读今晚的结果。

sentences.en: After the election, when you wake up, what are the headlines that you are hoping to see?
sentences.zh: 选举结束后，当你醒来时，你最希望看到的头条新闻是什么？

sentences.en: A red wave.
sentences.zh: 红色浪潮。

sentences.en: That there is no big blue wave.
sentences.zh: 没有所谓的蓝色浪潮。

sentences.en: Good God, I'm hoping that this predicted blue wave is actually a real thing.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我希望预测的蓝色浪潮真的能实现。

sentences.en: The blue wave that everyone's predicting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在预测的蓝色浪潮。

sentences.en: I would love to see that headline.
sentences.zh: 我很想看到那个头条。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, November 3rd, Election Day.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月3日星期二，选举日。

sentences.en: Nate.
sentences.zh: 内特。

sentences.en: Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔。

sentences.en: Happy Election Day.
sentences.zh: 选举日快乐。

sentences.en: Happy Election Day.
sentences.zh: 选举日快乐。

sentences.en: To you, and to all who celebrate.
sentences.zh: 祝你，也祝所有庆祝这一天的人快乐。

sentences.en: To every American voter, happy Election Day.
sentences.zh: 祝每一位美国选民，选举日快乐。

sentences.en: So, Nate, we are here today to do something we started doing with you a few elections ago, which is to offer our listeners a roadmap to election night.
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，我们今天来到这里，是为了做一件我们几年前就开始和你一起做的事，那就是为我们的听众提供一份选举之夜的路线图。

sentences.en: Because starting around 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 因为从今晚7点左右开始，

sentences.en: Eastern tonight, everyone's screens are going to be bombarded with projections and breaking news alerts.
sentences.zh: 东部时间，每个人的屏幕都将被预测结果和突发新闻提醒所轰炸。

sentences.en: This person won this House seat.
sentences.zh: 这个人赢得了这个众议院席位。

sentences.en: This person lost that Senate seat.
sentences.zh: 那个人输掉了那个参议院席位。

sentences.en: And it's always cacophonous, a little confusing.
sentences.zh: 这总是让人感到嘈杂，甚至有点困惑。

sentences.en: And so, we want to give people a user's guide to the entire night with you as our guide, our captain, whichever.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们想以你为向导、队长，或者随便什么称呼，给人们提供一份整晚的指南。

sentences.en: Do you have a preferred metaphor?
sentences.zh: 你有喜欢的隐喻吗？

sentences.en: Preferred metaphor.
sentences.zh: 喜欢的隐喻。

sentences.en: Captain will work.
sentences.zh: 队长就行。

sentences.en: And you come armed, Captain, with a new round of polling that the Times completed over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 队长，你还带来了《时报》周末完成的一轮新民调。

sentences.en: So, it's as up-to-date as imaginable.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是目前能想象到的最新数据。

sentences.en: So, start with that new data.
sentences.zh: 那么，从那个新数据开始吧。

sentences.en: So, stepping back briefly, as we've said on the show before, the Democrats are overwhelming favorites to take the House.
sentences.zh: 简单回顾一下，正如我们在节目中之前所说，民主党是赢得众议院的绝对热门。

sentences.en: The big question in this election is whether they can win the Senate, where they need to win at least two seats that Donald Trump won by double digits.
sentences.zh: 这次选举的大问题是他们能否赢得参议院，在那里他们需要赢得至少两个特朗普曾以两位数优势获胜的席位。

sentences.en: That's a tough feat.
sentences.zh: 那是一项艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: Our final polls of the seven states' likeliest to decide the Senate show the Democrats ahead, even if sometimes only narrowly, in all seven of those races.
sentences.zh: 我们对最有可能决定参议院归属的七个州的最终民调显示，民主党在所有这七场竞选中都处于领先地位，尽管有时优势微弱。

sentences.en: That's Michigan, Maine, Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Iowa, and Alaska.
sentences.zh: 那就是密歇根州、缅因州、得克萨斯州、俄亥俄州、堪萨斯州、艾奥瓦州和阿拉斯加州。

sentences.en: Five of those states, by the way, voted for Trump by double digits.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，其中五个州在上次选举中特朗普以两位数优势获胜。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The polls are exactly right, and they never are, of course.
sentences.zh: 民调完全准确，当然，它们从来没准过。

sentences.en: But if they are, that would be enough for Democrats to take the chamber and have an election that they wouldn't have even imagined a year ago.
sentences.zh: 但如果它们准了，那将足以让民主党夺取参议院，并取得一场他们一年前甚至无法想象的胜利。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this was, we should just say, polling largely conducted before two pretty dramatic political surprises over the past week.
sentences.zh: 我们应该说明，这些民调主要是在过去一周发生两起相当戏剧性的政治意外之前进行的。

sentences.en: We had a Times investigation into the Alaska Senate race that showed that the Democratic nominee, Mary Peltola's campaign,
sentences.zh: 《时报》对阿拉斯加参议院竞选的调查显示，民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉的竞选团队，

sentences.en: played a role in recruiting a spoiler candidate, a second Dan Sullivan.
sentences.zh: 在招募一名搅局候选人，即第二个丹·沙利文方面发挥了作用。

sentences.en: And then after that, as if that wasn't dramatic enough, we had the losing Democratic primary candidate in the Michigan Senate race,
sentences.zh: 在那之后，仿佛这还不够戏剧性，密歇根州参议院竞选中的落败民主党初选候选人，

sentences.en: Haley Stevens, snub the Democratic nominee, Abdul Asayyad, and cross party lines and endorse his Republican rival, Mike Rogers.
sentences.zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯，冷落了民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·阿萨亚德，跨越党派界限支持了他的共和党对手迈克·罗杰斯。

sentences.en: Did the polling tell us anything about whether either of those two soap operas might matter in those two races?
sentences.zh: 民调有没有告诉我们这两场肥皂剧是否会对那两场竞选产生影响？

sentences.en: In a certain sense, the poll in Michigan found Dr. Al-Sayed up by 11 points.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，密歇根州的民调显示阿尔-萨耶德博士领先11个百分点。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which is his largest lead of the cycle, a six-point gain from our last poll in September.
sentences.zh: 这是他本周期内最大的领先优势，比我们9月份的民调增长了6个百分点。

sentences.en: Seemingly undentable, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 看起来似乎无法撼动。

sentences.en: And that would seem undentable.
sentences.zh: 那看起来确实无法撼动。

sentences.en: Haley Stevens endorsing his rival.
sentences.zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯支持了他的对手。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In this political environment, with Donald Trump as unpopular as he is, it seems like Michigan Democrats and Democratic-leaning voters are going to get behind Dr. Al-Sayed,
sentences.zh: 在这种政治环境下，考虑到唐纳德·特朗普如此不受欢迎，看起来密歇根州的民主党人和倾向民主党的选民会支持阿尔-萨耶德博士，

sentences.en: if our poll is right.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的民调是正确的话。

sentences.en: Alaska.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加。

sentences.en: Alaska is a pretty different story.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加的情况则完全不同。

sentences.en: That's a race where Mary Peltola only led by one point.
sentences.zh: 在那场竞选中，玛丽·佩尔托拉仅领先一个百分点。

sentences.en: And that was a- In our final poll.
sentences.zh: 那是在——在我们最后的民调中。

sentences.en: In our final poll.
sentences.zh: 在我们最后的民调中。

sentences.en: That was a decline from a seven-point lead in our penultimate poll.
sentences.zh: 这比我们倒数第二次民调中七个百分点的领先优势有所下降。

sentences.en: She has had other issues in this campaign about a month ago.
sentences.zh: 她在这次竞选中大约一个月前还有其他问题。

sentences.en: The Times reported that she had potentially mistreated staff members.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称她可能虐待了员工。

sentences.en: So the trend line there is sort of working in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 所以那里的趋势线有点朝着错误的方向发展。

sentences.en: And now here's what may be a final push that could potentially help her Republican rival get over the top.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能是最后的一击，可能会帮助她的共和党对手反超。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: But still, Peltola is leading in that poll just not by much at all.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，佩尔托拉在民调中仍然领先，只是优势非常微弱。

sentences.en: Not by much.
sentences.zh: 优势不大。

sentences.en: I think that race is a true toss if you take our data on its face.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果直接看我们的数据，那场竞选确实是五五开。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But all in all, a very positive poll for Democrats across these seven key Senate races that could determine which party controls that chamber.
sentences.zh: 但总而言之，对于民主党来说，这七个关键参议院席位的民调非常积极，这可能决定哪个党派控制参议院。

sentences.en: Let's now incorporate that into our roadmap for election night.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们把它纳入我们的选举之夜路线图。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, you know, as I mentioned, it's sort of inevitable that the Democrats are going to take the House this year.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，正如我提到的，民主党今年夺取众议院几乎是不可避免的。

sentences.en: And one way to think about that is in terms of a metaphor that people love to use in midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 考虑这一点的一种方式是使用人们在中期选举中喜欢用的隐喻。

sentences.en: And that's the idea of a blue wave.
sentences.zh: 那就是蓝色浪潮的概念。

sentences.en: There's no formal definition of a blue wave.
sentences.zh: 蓝色浪潮没有正式的定义。

sentences.en: You know it when you see it.
sentences.zh: 当你看到它时，你就知道了。

sentences.en: You do know it when you see it.
sentences.zh: 当你看到它时，你确实会知道。

sentences.en: But some kind of blue wave is inevitable in this election.
sentences.zh: 但在这次选举中，某种蓝色浪潮是不可避免的。

sentences.en: That's the reason why a Democratic House seems essentially inevitable in this election.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么民主党控制众议院在这次选举中看起来基本不可避免的原因。

sentences.en: But the big question is whether that wave will be big enough to yield major Democratic breakthroughs,
sentences.zh: 但大问题是，这股浪潮是否足够大，能带来民主党的重大突破，

sentences.en: even in districts and states that voted for Trump by double digits to give them that feeling of a sweeping victory.
sentences.zh: 即使是在特朗普曾以两位数优势获胜的选区和州，也能给他们带来那种大获全胜的感觉。

sentences.en: In potentially both chambers.
sentences.zh: 可能是在两个议院中。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: So in that sense, Michael, I see four basic scenarios for what might unfold on election night.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，迈克尔，我看到了选举之夜可能展开的四种基本情景。

sentences.en: All four involve blue waves, but they're of different heights and they will leave Democrats or Republicans feeling very differently when all the votes are counted.
sentences.zh: 所有四种情景都涉及蓝色浪潮，但它们的高度不同，当所有选票统计完毕时，民主党人或共和党人的感受将截然不同。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's talk through these four wave-ish scenarios.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈这四种浪潮情景。

sentences.en: Let's start with the first one.
sentences.zh: 让我们从第一个开始。

sentences.en: I think the first scenario is that the Republicans in heavily Republican districts stay dry.
sentences.zh: 我认为第一种情景是，共和党在共和党势力强大的选区保持干燥。

sentences.en: So you're really going to commit to the bit here?
sentences.zh: 所以你真的要坚持这个比喻到底吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to commit to the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 我要坚持这个隐喻。

sentences.en: You're a Republican on a cliff.
sentences.zh: 你是一个站在悬崖上的共和党人。

sentences.en: The big blue wave crashes ashore.
sentences.zh: 巨大的蓝色浪潮冲上岸边。

sentences.en: It's as big as any wave you've ever seen.
sentences.zh: 它和你见过的任何浪潮一样大。

sentences.en: But it doesn't reach you way up at your height, way in these Trump plus 10 districts.
sentences.zh: 但它没有到达你所在的高处，那些特朗普领先10个百分点的选区。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么会？

sentences.en: How does that not reach them?
sentences.zh: 它怎么会触及不到他们？

sentences.en: Well, one factor is that the Republicans have redrawn the nation's congressional maps to their advantage over the last year.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个因素是共和党在过去一年里为了自身利益重新划分了全国的国会选区地图。

sentences.en: You can think of that as Republican mapmakers evacuating their members away from the shoreline into high ground.
sentences.zh: 你可以认为这是共和党地图绘制者将他们的成员从海岸线疏散到高地。

sentences.en: So they would have been knocked out if it weren't for redistricting.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为重新划分选区，他们本会被淘汰。

sentences.en: Now they're way up above the wave.
sentences.zh: 现在他们远在浪潮之上。

sentences.en: Maybe they can survive this year.
sentences.zh: 也许他们今年能幸存下来。

sentences.en: The Senate's a little bit of a different story.
sentences.zh: 参议院的情况则有点不同。

sentences.en: There just aren't that many seats up for grabs in any particular year.
sentences.zh: 在任何特定年份，可供争夺的席位其实并不多。

sentences.en: Only one-third of the seats are at stake.
sentences.zh: 只有三分之一的席位面临改选。

sentences.en: And it so happens that this year there aren't very many vulnerable Republican seats up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，今年并没有多少共和党人的脆弱席位可供争夺。

sentences.en: So as I mentioned earlier, the Democrats will have to flip at least two states that voted for Trump by at least double digits.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，民主党人必须至少拿下两个特朗普曾以两位数优势获胜的州。

sentences.en: They'll have to win at least two states that are on high ground.
sentences.zh: 他们必须赢得至少两个处于高地的州。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The map was inherently challenging for Democrats to begin with.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，这张选票地图对民主党人来说就极具挑战性。

sentences.en: Gerrymandering helped make it even more challenging.
sentences.zh: 选区划分不公让情况变得更加严峻。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure I understand what the results of scenario one look like in the House and in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保自己理解情景一在众议院和参议院的结果会是什么样。

sentences.en: In the House, the Democrats win, but maybe only by a modest margin, a handful of seats.
sentences.zh: 在众议院，民主党人获胜，但优势可能很小，仅多出少数几个席位。

sentences.en: In the Senate, they don't really come all that close to flipping the chamber.
sentences.zh: 在参议院，他们实际上并没有那么接近夺取控制权。

sentences.en: Some of the states that we've been talking about is potentially competitive like Kansas or Iowa, South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论的一些潜在竞争激烈的州，比如堪萨斯州、艾奥瓦州或南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: They don't end up that close on election night.
sentences.zh: 选举之夜结束时，它们并没有那么接近。

sentences.en: They just go to the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 它们最终还是归了共和党。

sentences.en: They just go to the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 它们最终还是归了共和党。

sentences.en: And that could be clear pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 这一点很快就能看得很清楚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What would be the signs of that as the clock starts to tick into the evening hours on Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 随着周二傍晚时钟滴答作响，会有什么迹象表明这一点呢？

sentences.en: With one big caveat that I'll get to in a second.
sentences.zh: 有一个重要的前提，我稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: When the polls close in Kentucky and Indiana at 6 p.m.
sentences.zh: 当肯塔基州和印第安纳州的投票站在下午6点关闭时，

sentences.en: and then later across the southeast at 7 p.m.,
sentences.zh: 随后在晚上7点，整个东南部地区的投票站也会关闭，

sentences.en: there will be over a dozen of these districts that are either highly competitive or that voted for Trump by double digits that we'll be watching.
sentences.zh: 我们将关注十几个竞争极其激烈或特朗普曾以两位数优势获胜的选区。

sentences.en: Where we'll quickly get a sense of whether the Republicans really are vulnerable in these heavily Republican seats like the polls have suggested I'll cycle.
sentences.zh: 我们将很快了解到，共和党人在这些深红选区是否真的像民调显示的那样脆弱。

sentences.en: Give us some examples of these places.
sentences.zh: 给我们举几个这些地方的例子。

sentences.en: The first one would be Kentucky's 6th district.
sentences.zh: 第一个是肯塔基州第六选区。

sentences.en: It's around Lexington.
sentences.zh: 它位于列克星敦附近。

sentences.en: It voted for Trump by 15 points.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在那里以15个百分点的优势获胜。

sentences.en: That race is considered a toss-up.
sentences.zh: 那场竞选被认为胜负难料。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And it's a Trump plus 15 district.
sentences.zh: 而且那是一个特朗普领先15个百分点的选区。

sentences.en: So all the Republicans need to do to win this is just get Republicans to come back on board.
sentences.zh: 所以共和党人要赢得这个选区，只需要让共和党选民回归即可。

sentences.en: And we'll know pretty quickly whether Kentucky 6 is a real race or whether actually Republicans are going to show up, vote, and vote Republican.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就会知道肯塔基第六选区是否真的是一场势均力敌的较量，还是说共和党人真的会出来投票，并投给共和党。

sentences.en: Later on, there's a whole slew of those gerrymandered districts in North Carolina and Florida that the Republicans have redrawn to be around Trump plus 10.
sentences.zh: 稍后，北卡罗来纳州和佛罗里达州还有一大批经过重新划分的选区，共和党人将这些选区重划为特朗普领先约10个百分点。

sentences.en: Democrats are hoping to hold some of them.
sentences.zh: 民主党人希望能守住其中一些。

sentences.en: We'll see it soon after 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 晚上7点过后不久我们就会看到，

sentences.en: whether the Republicans succeeded in flipping those districts or not and whether they did so with room to spare.
sentences.zh: 共和党人是否成功翻转了这些选区，以及他们是否赢得游刃有余。

sentences.en: And then we'll also have the Senate races in South Carolina and Florida.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还将关注南卡罗来纳州和佛罗里达州的参议院竞选。

sentences.en: Republicans are expected to win those races.
sentences.zh: 预计共和党人会赢得这些竞选。

sentences.en: But if they win them comfortably by, say, nearly 10 points like they usually would,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们像往常一样以比如近10个百分点的优势轻松获胜，

sentences.en: that would be a sign that Republicans have come home and that the worst-case scenario for Republicans in this election might not materialize.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个信号，表明共和党选民已经回归，共和党人在这次选举中最坏的情况可能不会发生。

sentences.en: I do need to have one big warning, though, here.
sentences.zh: 不过，我确实需要在这里给出一个重要的警告。

sentences.en: Which is?
sentences.zh: 是什么？

sentences.en: Which is that although we'll know relatively quickly whether the Republicans have held these seats.
sentences.zh: 那就是，虽然我们能相对较快地知道共和党人是否守住了这些席位。

sentences.en: Whether they're dry.
sentences.zh: 是否稳操胜券。

sentences.en: Whether they're dry.
sentences.zh: 是否稳操胜券。

sentences.en: We are going to have a moment just before then when it looks like this election could be really, really blue.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，我们会有片刻时间看起来这次选举可能会呈现出一片“深蓝”。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is the early vote.
sentences.zh: 原因就是提前投票。

sentences.en: It is very clear that the Democrats have done exceptionally well in the early vote.
sentences.zh: 很明显，民主党人在提前投票中表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: It is also possible, however, and we've seen this happen before, like in 2020 or 2016, that Republicans just show up to vote on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们也曾见过这种情况，比如2020年或2016年，共和党人可能只是在选举日当天出来投票。

sentences.en: In most of the states we've been talking about, the early vote gets counted firSt.
sentences.zh: 在我们讨论的大多数州，提前投票会先被统计。

sentences.en: The Democrats could be looking really, really good.
sentences.zh: 民主党人看起来可能会非常、非常有利。

sentences.en: And then the Election Day vote could come in and leave them disappointed.
sentences.zh: 然后选举日的选票一出来，可能会让他们感到失望。

sentences.en: So this is a blue mirage.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种“蓝色海市蜃楼”。

sentences.en: Don't be surprised for 45 minutes for Democrats to be leading in Florida and South Carolina, even if they're actually going to lose.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人在佛罗里达州和南卡罗来纳州领先45分钟，即使他们最终会输，也不要感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So we have to wait at least a little bit to see that Election Day vote before we can determine the direction that the night is heading.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须至少等待一会儿，看看选举日的投票情况，才能确定当晚的走向。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: Nate, if Scenario 1 comes to pass, it will have inevitably meant that there was systemic polling error of some kind.
sentences.zh: 内特，如果情景一发生，那不可避免地意味着某种系统性的民调误差。

sentences.en: And you're our chief in-house pollster.
sentences.zh: 你是我们的首席内部民调专家。

sentences.en: So just help us understand a world where the polls are so off that you get Scenario 1.
sentences.zh: 所以请帮我们理解一个民调如此失准以至于出现情景一的世界。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's important to be clear about this.
sentences.zh: 是的，这一点必须说清楚。

sentences.en: At this point, Scenario 1 would absolutely require a polling error on the scale of 2016 or 2020, and maybe even beyond that, Michael.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，情景一绝对需要达到2016年或2020年规模的民调误差，甚至可能更大，迈克尔。

sentences.en: I do think that it is conceivable.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是可以想象的。

sentences.en: We know in general that Trump's supporters are less likely to respond to polls.
sentences.zh: 我们普遍知道，特朗普的支持者不太可能回应民调。

sentences.en: Pollsters try and do things to adjust for this, and in some cycles it seems to work, and in some cycles it does not.
sentences.zh: 民调机构试图采取措施来调整这一点，在某些周期似乎有效，而在某些周期则不然。

sentences.en: The other factor here that I think raises the potential for a polling error even more is that we're really focused on heavily Republican states and districts.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个增加民调误差可能性的因素是，我们非常关注共和党占优势的州和选区。

sentences.en: And this creates a risk to pollsters where even if they're right about what voters are thinking now,
sentences.zh: 这给民调机构带来了一种风险，即使他们对选民现在的想法判断正确，

sentences.en: there's this possibility that in the end Republicans just do what they usually do.
sentences.zh: 但最终共和党人还是会做他们通常会做的事情。

sentences.en: They can come out and vote.
sentences.zh: 他们会出来投票。

sentences.en: And look,
sentences.zh: 而且你看，

sentences.en: I don't doubt that there are millions of Republican voters today who are deeply dissatisfied with President Trump and don't even like the Republican nominee in their state.
sentences.zh: 我不怀疑今天有数百万共和党选民对特朗普总统深感不满，甚至不喜欢他们所在州的共和党候选人。

sentences.en: And they are expressing that dissatisfaction to pollsters.
sentences.zh: 他们正在向民调机构表达这种不满。

sentences.en: But it remains to be seen when they show up in a voting booth whether they're really going to vote for a Democrat like they say.
sentences.zh: 但当他们走进投票站时，是否真的会像他们说的那样投票给民主党，还有待观察。

sentences.en: If they do not, which I think in today's polarized era just can't be too surprising, you would quickly see these Republican-leaning districts snap back to the right.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没有这样做，我认为在当今两极分化的时代这并不令人惊讶，你会很快看到这些倾向共和党的选区迅速向右转。

sentences.en: And I think that's the biggest risk to pollsters in this election.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是这次选举中民调机构面临的最大风险。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not that they will have misled pollsters.
sentences.zh: 并不是他们误导了民调机构。

sentences.en: In a certain sense, they may have misled themselves momentarily.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，他们可能暂时误导了自己。

sentences.en: And once Election Day rolls around, they come home to the familiar home of the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 一旦选举日到来，他们就会回到共和党这个熟悉的家。

sentences.en: I think that's a real possibility.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种真实的可能性。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's scenario one.
sentences.zh: 这就是情景一。

sentences.en: It's extremely good for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这对共和党人来说极其有利。

sentences.en: They'll be thrilled.
sentences.zh: 他们会欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: Extremely bad for pollsters.
sentences.zh: 对民调机构来说极其糟糕。

sentences.en: Let's talk about scenario two.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈情景二。

sentences.en: Scenario two is where the Republicans don't stay dry.
sentences.zh: 情景二是共和党人没有“稳操胜券”。

sentences.en: Get really wet.
sentences.zh: 而是被彻底淋湿了。

sentences.en: The wave reaches them high up on the cliff.
sentences.zh: 浪潮冲击到了悬崖高处。

sentences.en: The wave is every bit as big as the pollsters said it would.
sentences.zh: 浪潮正如民调机构所说的那样巨大。

sentences.en: The Democrats win the House and they win it big.
sentences.zh: 民主党人赢得了众议院，而且是大胜。

sentences.en: But in the critical states where Donald Trump won by 10 points or more, the Republicans hold on.
sentences.zh: 但在唐纳德·特朗普以10个百分点或更多优势获胜的关键州，共和党人守住了阵地。

sentences.en: So in the first scenario, a race like South Carolina Senate may not even be close at all.
sentences.zh: 所以在第一种情景中，像南卡罗来纳州参议院这样的竞选可能根本不会很接近。

sentences.en: That's the race where Darlene Graham, Lindsey Graham's sister,
sentences.zh: 那就是达琳·格雷厄姆，也就是林赛·格雷厄姆的妹妹参加的那场竞选，

sentences.en: is running in what seems to be a surprisingly close race in a state that is never really competitive in federal elections.
sentences.zh: 在一个联邦选举中从未真正具有竞争力的州，这场竞选看起来出人意料地接近。

sentences.en: In this one, it really is close.
sentences.zh: 在这种情景下，它确实很接近。

sentences.en: But in this scenario, Darlene Graham wins.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情景下，达琳·格雷厄姆赢了。

sentences.en: And the same story would play out in Iowa and in Kansas and maybe in Ohio and enough states that the Republicans ultimately retain control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 同样的故事也会在艾奥瓦州、堪萨斯州，也许还有俄亥俄州以及足够多的州上演，最终共和党人保留了参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: In this scenario, we will have to wait much longer on election night before we understand that the Republicans have retained control of the chamber.
sentences.zh: 在这种情景下，我们必须在选举之夜等待更久，才能明白共和党人已经保留了对参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: Because unfortunately, most of the key Senate states do not close their polls early on election night.
sentences.zh: 因为不幸的是，大多数关键的参议院州在选举之夜并没有提前关闭投票站。

sentences.en: So it might only become clear that the Republicans are favored by maybe midnight.
sentences.zh: 所以可能要到午夜左右，共和党人占优的情况才会变得明朗。

sentences.en: And worse still, if it's really close, there are two states, Maine and Alaska, or I'm not sure we're going to know the answer for days in this scenario.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，如果选情非常胶着，有两个州，缅因州和阿拉斯加州，我不确定在这种情景下我们几天内能否知道结果。

sentences.en: Both states take a really long time to count their vote.
sentences.zh: 这两个州统计选票都需要很长时间。

sentences.en: Maine counts their vote in much of the state by hand.
sentences.zh: 缅因州大部分地区的选票是手工统计的。

sentences.en: And in recent elections, 20% of the vote is still uncounted at noon on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 在最近的选举中，周三中午仍有20%的选票未统计。

sentences.en: Alaska, I think, has a better excuse, which is that it has this huge far-flung population that's voting by mail.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加州，我想有一个更好的借口，那就是它有大量分散的人口通过邮寄投票。

sentences.en: But that takes them a week to count.
sentences.zh: 但这需要他们一周的时间来统计。

sentences.en: And as if all of this isn't enough, there's then a second wrinkle in both of these states.
sentences.zh: 而且好像这一切还不够，这两个州还有第二个复杂之处。

sentences.en: They both have rank choice voting.
sentences.zh: 它们都实行排序复选制投票。

sentences.en: So once they've counted all the votes, then they have to do the rank choice vote if no one reaches 50%, which in this scenario is quite plausible.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦他们统计完所有选票，如果没人达到50%，他们就必须进行排序复选投票，在这种情景下这很可能发生。

sentences.en: That's the second round of counting.
sentences.zh: 那是第二轮计票。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so, like, in Alaska, I think that's November 18th.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如在阿拉斯加州，我想那是11月18日。

sentences.en: So in this scenario— I just want people to see the pained look on your face right now.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情景下——我只是想让大家看看你现在脸上痛苦的表情。

sentences.en: You said happy election.
sentences.zh: 你说“选举快乐”。

sentences.en: You should really be saying happy race call day.
sentences.zh: 你真的应该说“选举结果公布日快乐”。

sentences.en: Because in this scenario where the Republicans narrowly hang on,
sentences.zh: 因为在这种共和党人勉强守住的情景下，

sentences.en: it would be a really long time before they had run the table in each of these critical states that they're endangering.
sentences.zh: 在他们完成所有这些关键州的计票之前，还需要很长一段时间。

sentences.en: So basically, in scenario number two, Democrats get very close to winning the Senate, but the cards just don't break their way in enough of these red states.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，在情景二中，民主党人非常接近赢得参议院，但选票在足够多的红州没有向他们倾斜。

sentences.en: Too many Republican candidates win these seemingly competitive Senate contests, and at the end of the day, they keep control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 太多的共和党候选人赢得了这些看似竞争激烈的参议院竞选，最终，他们保住了参议院的控制权。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I want to note, scenario two, by historical measures, could still be an extraordinary night for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我想指出，按历史标准衡量，情景二对民主党人来说仍然可能是一个非凡的夜晚。

sentences.en: It could be the best performance that the party has had in red states in decades.
sentences.zh: 这可能是该党几十年来在红州表现最好的一次。

sentences.en: Like, I think it's conceivable Democrats could win Texas in this scenario.
sentences.zh: 比如，我认为民主党人在这种情景下赢得得克萨斯州是可以想象的。

sentences.en: Or maybe it's Kansas.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是堪萨斯州。

sentences.en: And any of them, by historic standards, would really be impressive.
sentences.zh: 按历史标准来看，任何一个州的结果都会令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: But the critical thing about this scenario is it just doesn't add up to 51 seats for them,
sentences.zh: 但这种情景的关键在于，它无法让他们获得51个席位，

sentences.en: which is what's ultimately going to determine whether they're thrilled by the ultimate outcome or not.
sentences.zh: 这最终将决定他们是否对最终结果感到欣喜。

sentences.en: And ultimately, given the expectations, I suspect Democrats would be deeply disappointed, and regardless, it would be an incredibly late night.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，考虑到预期，我怀疑民主党人会深感失望，无论如何，那将是一个极其漫长的夜晚。

sentences.en: So let's, Nate, move on to the third scenario.
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，让我们进入第三种情景。

sentences.en: In a lot of ways, scenario three is a lot like scenario two.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，情景三和情景二非常相似。

sentences.en: The wave is basically as big.
sentences.zh: 浪潮基本上一样大。

sentences.en: The Republicans are all wet.
sentences.zh: 共和党人全都“湿透了”。

sentences.en: But in scenario three, the Republicans' sandbags fail.
sentences.zh: 但在情景三中，共和党人的沙袋失效了。

sentences.en: The wave swamps them.
sentences.zh: 浪潮淹没了他们。

sentences.en: And in these critical Senate races, the Democrats do flip the seats they need to take control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 在这些关键的参议院竞选中，民主党人确实翻转了他们夺取参议院控制权所需的席位。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So key difference between three and two is that the Democrats do take the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以三和二的关键区别在于民主党人确实拿下了参议院。

sentences.en: But by how much?
sentences.zh: 但赢了多少？

sentences.en: To me, what's unique about scenario three is that these states are all really close.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，情景三的独特之处在于这些州的选情都非常接近。

sentences.en: And the difference between scenario three and scenario two could be tens of thousands of votes in Alaska and in Ohio and so on.
sentences.zh: 情景三和情景二的区别可能在于阿拉斯加州、俄亥俄州等地数万张选票的差距。

sentences.en: And in one, they break one way, and in the other, they break toward the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 在一种情景中，它们向一个方向倾斜，而在另一种情景中，它们向民主党倾斜。

sentences.en: I think that the best case for Democrats in this scenario might be something like 53 seats in the Senate, maybe even 54, though I think that would be pretty lucky.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这种情景下，民主党人的最好情况可能是获得参议院53个席位，甚至54个，尽管我认为那会非常幸运。

sentences.en: But it could be as little as 51.
sentences.zh: 但也可能少至51个。

sentences.en: They could just barely scratch by with the bare minimum necessary to take the chamber.
sentences.zh: 他们可能只是勉强达到夺取参议院控制权所需的最低限度。

sentences.en: As long as they do that, I think the Democrats will ultimately feel elated by the night, even if it is a disappointment compared to, you know,
sentences.zh: 只要他们做到了，我认为民主党人最终会对这个夜晚感到欣喜，即使与那些比这更高期望的民调相比，这是一种失望，

sentences.en: polls that have raised even higher expectations than that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的。

sentences.en: What will be the indication that a scenario three is unfolding versus a scenario two?
sentences.zh: 什么迹象表明情景三正在展开，而不是情景二？

sentences.en: Because, as you say, the waves may not feel all that different in scale.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，浪潮在规模上可能感觉并没有太大不同。

sentences.en: So when would we know the difference?
sentences.zh: 那么我们什么时候才能知道区别呢？

sentences.en: I think that there are really two paths for how we could feel the difference.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对这种差异的感受确实有两条路径。

sentences.en: One of them is where Democrats win on election night in enough of these states that do count their votes quickly enough.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是民主党在选举之夜在足够多计票迅速的州获胜。

sentences.en: Texas, Ohio, Iowa, Kansas.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州、俄亥俄州、爱荷华州、堪萨斯州。

sentences.en: If the Democrats are winning those states, we could have a decision on election night.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党在这些州获胜，我们可能在选举之夜就能得出结果。

sentences.en: It may be late on election night.
sentences.zh: 可能是在选举之夜的深夜。

sentences.en: But we'll know that the Democrats have taken the House and the Senate.
sentences.zh: 但我们会知道民主党已经拿下了众议院和参议院。

sentences.en: And the House and the Senate.
sentences.zh: 众议院和参议院。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If the Democrats depend on Maine or Alaska to do it, we're still stuck waiting.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党要靠缅因州或阿拉斯加州才能做到，那我们还得继续等。

sentences.en: So, from a purely selfish point of view, let's hope we have resolutions quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以，从纯粹自私的角度来看，让我们希望结果能尽快出来吧。

sentences.en: If it's going to happen, let it happen faSt.
sentences.zh: 如果注定要发生，那就让它快点发生吧。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's take a quick break.
sentences.zh: 我们先休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, come to the fourth, final, and I believe the most dramatic political scenario.
sentences.zh: 回来之后，我们将讨论第四个、最后一个，也是我认为最戏剧性的政治场景。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Of Tuesday night.
sentences.zh: 周二晚上的。

sentences.en: It would be something that we haven't seen in American politics in a long time.
sentences.zh: 这将是我们很久以来在美国政治中未曾见过的景象。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，你每天也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助你了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Neat.
sentences.zh: 真不错。

sentences.en: The fourth scenario for Tuesday night.
sentences.zh: 周二晚上的第四种场景。

sentences.en: The fourth scenario is the tsunami.
sentences.zh: 第四种场景是海啸。

sentences.en: It's where the life jackets and the sandbags never really had a chance.
sentences.zh: 那是救生衣和沙袋根本没机会发挥作用的情况。

sentences.en: You're on the cliff and the wave is way over your head.
sentences.zh: 你站在悬崖上，海浪已经高过你的头顶。

sentences.en: The Republicans are basically washed away.
sentences.zh: 共和党人基本上被冲走了。

sentences.en: They are inundated.
sentences.zh: 他们被淹没了。

sentences.en: Let me describe what the extent of the damage for Republicans could look like in this sort of scenario.
sentences.zh: 让我来描述一下在这种场景下，共和党人可能遭受的损失程度。

sentences.en: In the House, the Democrats could win the popular vote by double digits and claim 250 seats maybe.
sentences.zh: 在众议院，民主党可能以两位数的优势赢得普选，并可能获得250个席位。

sentences.en: In the Senate, the Republicans wouldn't merely lose in some close battles in a few critical states.
sentences.zh: 在参议院，共和党人不仅仅是在几个关键州的激烈竞争中失利。

sentences.en: The Democrats might win the Senate with room to spare.
sentences.zh: 民主党可能会以相当大的优势赢得参议院。

sentences.en: In a place like Michigan, where the Democrats have a candidate in Dr. El-Sayed that maybe could have lost in a different election.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州这样的地方，民主党有一位候选人埃尔-赛义德医生，他可能在另一场选举中会输。

sentences.en: Like maybe he cruises to that big double-digit win that our poll showed this weekend.
sentences.zh: 也许他能以我们周末民调显示的那种两位数优势轻松获胜。

sentences.en: Maybe Democrats win Texas.
sentences.zh: 也许民主党会赢得德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: And they don't just win Texas by a little bit, but they win it big.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不仅是小胜，而是大胜。

sentences.en: James Tallarico wins by five points or more with Hispanic voters surging 40-plus points toward the left.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·塔拉里科以五个百分点或更多的优势获胜，拉美裔选民向左倾斜超过40个百分点。

sentences.en: And maybe the Democrats win Kansas, a Senate state that hasn't voted Democratic since 1932.
sentences.zh: 也许民主党会赢得堪萨斯州，这是一个自1932年以来从未投票给民主党的参议院席位州。

sentences.en: Again, not just by a little bit, but by five points or more.
sentences.zh: 同样，不是小胜，而是以五个百分点或更多的优势获胜。

sentences.en: And maybe a whole extra tier of state that we haven't really considered top-tier battleground.
sentences.zh: 也许还有我们从未真正考虑过的一整层非顶级战场州。

sentences.en: Like South Carolina, which I've alluded to a few times, but also add to that Florida or Mississippi maybe.
sentences.zh: 比如南卡罗来纳州，我提到过几次，但也加上佛罗里达州或密西西比州。

sentences.en: The Democrats are spending money there.
sentences.zh: 民主党正在那里投入资金。

sentences.en: And maybe those are the states that wind up being the closest on election night.
sentences.zh: 也许这些州最终会成为选举之夜竞争最激烈的州。

sentences.en: States that we haven't even really considered to be top-tier contests.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至没把它们当作顶级竞争对手的州。

sentences.en: Stepping back, this is a generational victory.
sentences.zh: 退一步看，这是一场代际胜利。

sentences.en: This is the largest victory for either party in decades.
sentences.zh: 这是几十年来任何政党取得的最大胜利。

sentences.en: The Democrats would win more Senate seats in heavily Republican territory in this scenario than both 2008 and 2006 combined.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，民主党在共和党重镇赢得的参议院席位将超过2008年和2006年的总和。

sentences.en: And then more.
sentences.zh: 甚至更多。

sentences.en: I think you'd have to go back maybe to 1974, the election right after Watergate, to come up with something that felt this big.
sentences.zh: 我想你得追溯到1974年，也就是水门事件后的那场选举，才能找到感觉如此重大的事件。

sentences.en: Another major victory for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党的又一场重大胜利。

sentences.en: An enormous victory for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 民主党的巨大胜利。

sentences.en: We just haven't seen an election like this in a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我们很久没有见过这样的选举了。

sentences.en: Scenario four.
sentences.zh: 第四种场景。

sentences.en: Well, at this point, which of these scenarios seems most likely most plausible given the polling we've done, given the political environment we're in?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这一点上，考虑到我们所做的民调和我们所处的政治环境，哪种场景看起来最可能、最合理？

sentences.en: I will find it hard to ever say scenario four is likely in this polarized era and when all Republicans need to do to avert scenario four is show up and vote Republican.
sentences.zh: 在这个两极分化的时代，我很难说第四种场景是可能的，因为共和党人要避免第四种场景，只需要出来投票支持共和党就行了。

sentences.en: But I do have to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 但我必须对你诚实。

sentences.en: And that's that the polls, if anything, say that scenario four is the single likeliest outcome here.
sentences.zh: 那就是，如果说民调说明了什么，那就是第四种场景是目前最可能的结果。

sentences.en: Maybe scenario 3.7 is the likeliest outcome based in the polls.
sentences.zh: 也许基于民调，3.7场景是最可能的结果。

sentences.en: The polls don't show Republicans losing in South Carolina, for instance, to take a case that I had in scenario four.
sentences.zh: 例如，民调并没有显示共和党人在南卡罗来纳州会输，这只是我第四种场景中的一个案例。

sentences.en: But they do show Democrats winning all of these critical Senate states, as I mentioned at the beginning of the episode.
sentences.zh: 但正如我在节目开头提到的，民调确实显示民主党正在赢得所有这些关键的参议院席位州。

sentences.en: They also show them winning in these red states with room to spare sometimes, like Texas.
sentences.zh: 民调还显示他们在这些红州有时也能以相当大的优势获胜，比如德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: The final polls show James Tallarico ahead by a comfortable margin, not just our polls, but other polls.
sentences.zh: 最终民调显示詹姆斯·塔拉里科以舒适的优势领先，不仅是我们的民调，其他民调也是如此。

sentences.en: Same story in Kansas.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州的情况也一样。

sentences.en: And I want to note that it's not just the polls that say this.
sentences.zh: 我想指出，不仅仅是民调这么说。

sentences.en: It's the behavior of both parties.
sentences.zh: 这也是两党的行为所反映的。

sentences.en: We've already talked about how Democrats are spending in places like Mississippi and South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过民主党如何在密西西比州和南卡罗来纳州等地投入资金。

sentences.en: The Republicans have spent hundreds of millions of dollars in Texas this cycle.
sentences.zh: 共和党在本周期已经在德克萨斯州花费了数亿美元。

sentences.en: It's not because they think it's the state it's been in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 那不是因为他们认为德州还是过去那个德州。

sentences.en: Donald Trump has been to South Carolina three times in the last few weeks.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普在过去几周里去了三次南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: And not just because he likes Charleston.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为他喜欢查尔斯顿。

sentences.en: And not just because he loves Charleston, but because they appear to be in really serious trouble here.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为他热爱查尔斯顿，而是因为他们看起来真的陷入了严重的麻烦。

sentences.en: Now, maybe those efforts are going to work.
sentences.zh: 现在，也许这些努力会奏效。

sentences.en: Maybe hundreds of millions of dollars and Donald Trump going to the right place during the final stretch gets enough of those Republicans back on board to avert this.
sentences.zh: 也许数亿美元的投入和唐纳德·特朗普在最后冲刺阶段去到正确的地方，能让足够多的共和党人回心转意来避免这种情况。

sentences.en: But that is just not what the polling says today, even if it is conceivable that the polls will be wrong as they have been before.
sentences.zh: 但那绝不是今天民调所显示的结果，即使民调像以前一样出错也是可以想象的。

sentences.en: I'm hearing you say that even though you don't want to say scenario four is the likeliest, you kind of just did say that it's the likelieSt.
sentences.zh: 我听出来你的意思是，尽管你不想说第四种场景是最可能的，但你刚才其实已经说了它是最可能的。

sentences.en: Basically, you're saying that this fourth scenario would seem to be staring us in the face.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你是说这第四种场景似乎正摆在我们面前。

sentences.en: That's a great way to put it, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你总结得太好了。

sentences.en: If we were standing beside these Republicans in these Trump plus 10 states, this wave that we are staring at looks big enough to wipe us away right now.
sentences.zh: 如果我们站在这些特朗普领先10个百分点的州的共和党人身边，我们现在面对的这股浪潮看起来大到足以把我们冲走。

sentences.en: Now, if you've been on the beach before, you've seen that the waves crash and unpredictable waves and the wave that you think is going to be the biggest breaks early and so on.
sentences.zh: 如果你去过海滩，你就会看到海浪会破碎，会有不可预测的海浪，你认为最大的浪往往会提前破碎，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So we can't make a perfect prediction about what it's going to look like once this wave breaks on this Republican cliff of ours.
sentences.zh: 所以我们无法对这股浪潮冲击我们的共和党悬崖时会是什么样子做出完美的预测。

sentences.en: But that's what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 但看起来就是这样。

sentences.en: This is the point of the conversation where I feel it's incumbent to return to the question of polling error.
sentences.zh: 这是对话中我觉得有必要回到民调误差问题的时候了。

sentences.en: We mentioned it earlier, but we didn't really talk about it with much granularity.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到了它，但并没有深入探讨。

sentences.en: And as we talk about how big a wave might look to us, we're basing that almost entirely on polling.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论海浪对我们来说可能有多大时，我们几乎完全是基于民调。

sentences.en: Let's talk about why we don't think or the steps you have taken to mitigate against the risk that this longstanding trend of Republicans being less likely to answer the phone for pollsters,
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈为什么我们不认为，或者你采取了哪些步骤来减轻这种风险，即共和党人不太愿意接听民调电话的长期趋势，

sentences.en: Democrats more eager to talk to pollsters, why that isn't influencing this understanding that we've arrived at.
sentences.zh: 而民主党人更乐于与民调人员交谈，为什么这没有影响我们得出的这种理解。

sentences.en: So essentially every pollster is going much farther to try and adjust their samples to properly represent Trump supporters than they did in 2020 or 2016.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上每个民调机构都在走得更远，试图调整他们的样本，以比2020年或2016年更准确地代表特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: They, in particular, simply just give more weight to the Trump supporters who take their polls.
sentences.zh: 他们特别地，只是给予那些参与民调的特朗普支持者更多的权重。

sentences.en: So let's take an evenly divided state like Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们以宾夕法尼亚州这样一个势均力敌的州为例。

sentences.en: If I take a poll of Pennsylvania and Trump voters are 40 percent of the sample and we know they were 50 percent of the vote,
sentences.zh: 如果我做一个宾夕法尼亚州的民调，特朗普选民占样本的40%，而我们知道他们占选票的50%，

sentences.en: the typical pollster will make them 50 percent of the vote right now.
sentences.zh: 典型的民调机构现在会让他们占到选票的50%。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: It's a heavy handed approach.
sentences.zh: 这是一种强硬的方法。

sentences.en: I will also note that if the turnout is very blue for Democrats, you can at least talk yourself into a scenario where that's an overcorrection potentially.
sentences.zh: 我还要指出，如果投票率对民主党非常有利，你至少可以说服自己，这可能是一种矫枉过正。

sentences.en: So it's not a panacea, but it is a reason to think that the risks could be lower than before,
sentences.zh: 所以这不是万灵药，但这是一个有理由认为风险可能比以前更低的理由，

sentences.en: though I should caution that just because pollsters are doing more than before doesn't mean that the underlying problems facing pollsters didn't get worse.
sentences.zh: 尽管我应该提醒，仅仅因为民调机构做得比以前多，并不意味着民调机构面临的根本问题没有恶化。

sentences.en: Well, what specific steps have you all taken here at The Times to feel good about reaching enough Republicans, enough Trump supporters,
sentences.zh: 那么，你们《时报》采取了哪些具体步骤来确保能够接触到足够的共和党人，足够的特朗普支持者，

sentences.en: enough of the people who might ultimately show up on Tuesday and essentially wipe out some of these Democratic events?
sentences.zh: 以及足够多最终可能在周二出现并基本上抹去一些民主党优势的人？

sentences.en: Did you use this word feel comfortable right there?
sentences.zh: 你刚才用了“感觉舒服”这个词吗？

sentences.en: So at first I just have to reiterate, like, although we've taken steps that I'll work through in a second,
sentences.zh: 首先我必须重申，虽然我们已经采取了步骤，我稍后会详细说明，

sentences.en: there's no one can tell you that they know whether the polls are going to be right heading into an election.
sentences.zh: 没有人能告诉你他们知道民调在选举前是否会准确。

sentences.en: But to answer your question, there are a couple of things that we do differently, both from other pollsters and in some cases than what we've done in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 但回答你的问题，我们确实做了一些与众不同的事情，既不同于其他民调机构，在某些情况下也不同于我们过去所做的。

sentences.en: First, that we do everything we can to make sure we reach as many Trump voters as possible,
sentences.zh: 首先，我们尽一切努力确保我们尽可能多地接触到特朗普选民，

sentences.en: including by ensuring that in any given state we reach the correct number of registered Republicans.
sentences.zh: 包括确保在任何给定的州，我们都能接触到正确数量的注册共和党人。

sentences.en: This is a guarantee that other pollsters don't make.
sentences.zh: 这是其他民调机构不做出的保证。

sentences.en: It doesn't guarantee that our polls are right either,
sentences.zh: 这也不能保证我们的民调就是正确的，

sentences.en: but I think it's helpful to have as many of these voters as possible so you can do the best job you can at trying to make sure that the sample is represented.
sentences.zh: 但我认为尽可能多地拥有这些选民是有帮助的，这样你就可以尽最大努力确保样本具有代表性。

sentences.en: The second thing is we really do try pretty hard and in ways that I think are pretty unique to try and make sure we have the right kind of Trump supporter.
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，我们确实非常努力，而且以我认为非常独特的方式，试图确保我们拥有正确类型的特朗普支持者。

sentences.en: This is something that's different in this election, but basically for every respondent, we try and guess how likely they were to vote for Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这是这次选举中不同的地方，但基本上对于每一位受访者，我们都会尝试猜测他们投票给唐纳德·特朗普的可能性有多大。

sentences.en: And so with that in mind, we try and distinguish between the kind of Republican who maybe did vote for Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这一点，我们试图区分那种可能投票给妮基·黑利的共和党人。

sentences.en: Maybe they live in a college-educated neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 也许他们住在受过大学教育的社区。

sentences.en: Maybe they have a professional degree.
sentences.zh: 也许他们拥有专业学位。

sentences.en: Maybe they have a doctor's license.
sentences.zh: 也许他们有医生执照。

sentences.en: Or conversely, maybe they're a Trump donor, which would be a pretty good sign they're a Trump supporter.
sentences.zh: 或者相反，也许他们是特朗普的捐赠者，这会是一个很好的迹象，表明他们是特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: And we use that data to try and make sure that we don't merely have the right number of Republicans
sentences.zh: 我们利用这些数据来确保我们不仅拥有正确数量的共和党人，

sentences.en: or the right number of Trump voters, but the right kind to the extent that we can.
sentences.zh: 或者正确数量的特朗普选民，而且在我们可以做到的范围内，拥有正确类型的人。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, again, none of this is a guarantee of anything, but these are the kind of things that we've done that we hope give us a better chance.
sentences.zh: 所以，再说一次，这些都不能保证什么，但这些是我们所做的，我们希望这能给我们更好的机会。

sentences.en: And I'll note that our final polls, as blue as they were, would have been three points bluer.
sentences.zh: 我要指出，我们的最终民调，尽管看起来偏向民主党，但如果按照我们2024年和2022年使用的调查方法，它们会更偏向民主党三个百分点。

sentences.en: Three points bluer.
sentences.zh: 更偏向三个百分点。

sentences.en: On the survey methodology we used in 2024 and 2022.
sentences.zh: 按照我们在2024年和2022年使用的调查方法。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And our polls weren't that bad in 2024 and 2022.
sentences.zh: 而且我们的民调在2024年和2022年并不算太差。

sentences.en: They were pretty accurate.
sentences.zh: 它们相当准确。

sentences.en: They were pretty accurate.
sentences.zh: 它们相当准确。

sentences.en: More than accurate enough for the Democrats to take the Senate with room to spare if they were off in the same way they were that time.
sentences.zh: 如果它们像上次那样出现同样的偏差，对于民主党来说，这已经足够准确，足以让他们以相当大的优势拿下参议院。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Are you suggesting that you could be, in that sense, overweighting Republicans and underweighting Democrats, even in these results that are extremely good for Democrats?
sentences.zh: 你是在暗示，即使在这些对民主党极其有利的结果中，你可能也在某种意义上高估了共和党，低估了民主党吗？

sentences.en: I think that could is the important word here, as I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，我认为“可能”这个词在这里很重要。

sentences.en: We really don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道。

sentences.en: I know that's frustrating.
sentences.zh: 我知道这很令人沮丧。

sentences.en: But there have been elections, again, where the polls underestimate Democrats, and there have been elections where they overestimate them, even in the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 但即便是在特朗普时代，也曾出现过民调低估民主党的情况，当然也有高估他们的时候。

sentences.en: And in this tsunami scenario, yeah, I think people would look back and say, you know, the steps that the pollsters were doing to try and reach more Trump supporters,
sentences.zh: 如果真的出现海啸般的局面，我想人们回过头来看会说，民调机构为了争取更多特朗普支持者所采取的那些措施，

sentences.en: at least in this particular election, went too far.
sentences.zh: 至少在这次选举中，做得太过火了。

sentences.en: That in every effort to get as many Trump supporters as you can, you actually miss that a lot of them just weren't voting in this election.
sentences.zh: 为了尽可能多地争取特朗普支持者，你们实际上忽略了他们中的许多人根本没有参加这次投票。

sentences.en: I think people hearing us talk about polling, potential polling error, steps we're taking to avoid it, will be curious what the actual early vote already is telling us
sentences.zh: 我想听到我们讨论民调、潜在的民调误差以及我们为避免误差所采取的措施，人们会好奇目前的提前投票结果到底告诉了我们什么，

sentences.en: and how much that may be supporting or not the emphasis we're placing on something like the third or fourth scenario here.
sentences.zh: 以及这些结果在多大程度上支持或不支持我们对这里提到的第三或第四种情境的侧重。

sentences.en: The early vote looks really blue, Michael.
sentences.zh: 提前投票的结果看起来非常偏向民主党，迈克尔。

sentences.en: You should be prepared, as I mentioned earlier, for the Democrats to be leading in states like Florida and South Carolina in the 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，你应该做好心理准备，民主党可能会在佛罗里达州和南卡罗来纳州等地的晚上7点时段领先，

sentences.en: hour, even where they're ultimately expected to lose.
sentences.zh: 即便他们最终预计会输掉这些州。

sentences.en: But if the Republicans don't vote on Election Day in enormous numbers to counter that, then those states may not be leading Republican.
sentences.zh: 但如果共和党人没有在选举日大规模投票来反击，那么这些州可能就不会是共和党领先。

sentences.en: It may not be a blue mirage.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是所谓的“蓝色幻象”。

sentences.en: It may not be a blue mirage.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是所谓的“蓝色幻象”。

sentences.en: It may actually be the first sight of that real wave.
sentences.zh: 这实际上可能是那场真正浪潮的初现。

sentences.en: Or take Texas.
sentences.zh: 或者看看德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: Two-thirds of the vote has already been cast in Texas.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州三分之二的选票已经投出。

sentences.en: It's a big proportion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的比例。

sentences.en: And in our data, it looks really Democratic.
sentences.zh: 根据我们的数据，它看起来非常支持民主党。

sentences.en: Not only are young, Latino, and non-voters showing up in significant numbers in Texas,
sentences.zh: 不仅是年轻人、拉丁裔和非选民在德克萨斯州大量出现，

sentences.en: but at least in our data, the people who are choosing to show up are just systematically likelier to be Democratic or James Tallarico supporters.
sentences.zh: 而且至少在我们的数据中，那些选择出来投票的人系统性地更倾向于支持民主党或詹姆斯·塔拉里科。

sentences.en: So none of this proves anything.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都不能证明什么。

sentences.en: On Election Day, Republicans can counter it, and they have before.
sentences.zh: 在选举日，共和党人可以反击，他们以前也这样做过。

sentences.en: In 2020, they did.
sentences.zh: 2020年他们就做到了。

sentences.en: But at least to this point, I don't think the Democrats could have asked for too much more in terms of the turnout they have.
sentences.zh: 但至少到目前为止，我认为民主党在投票率方面已经无可挑剔了。

sentences.en: Obviously, scenarios one and two would be a huge disappointment to Democrats, but it would to some degree be a reversion to the norm.
sentences.zh: 显然，第一和第二种情境对民主党来说会是巨大的失望，但在某种程度上这会是一种回归常态。

sentences.en: It would be a typical midterm year where the party out of power does well, but it still looks a lot like our usual polarized country.
sentences.zh: 这将是一个典型的中期选举年，执政党表现不佳，但这看起来仍然很像我们通常两极分化的国家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Three and four, four especially, those don't feel familiar.
sentences.zh: 第三和第四种，尤其是第四种，感觉很不寻常。

sentences.en: They don't.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: They're something that we haven't seen in a long time.
sentences.zh: 这是我们很久没见过的景象。

sentences.en: It's been 16 years since a party won even one seat that voted for the other side by double digits in the prior presidential election.
sentences.zh: 距离上一次有政党赢得在上届总统选举中以两位数优势投给对方的选区，已经过去16年了。

sentences.en: In our polls, the Democrats are leading in five.
sentences.zh: 在我们的民调中，民主党在五个这样的选区领先。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So – It defies our understanding of our polarized era.
sentences.zh: 所以——这超出了我们对当前两极分化时代的理解。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: In this – And it's worth, again, coming back to the voters who will decide this election, and they're not the voters who usually decide our elections.
sentences.zh: 在这个——再次回到那些将决定这次选举的选民身上是值得的，他们不是通常决定我们选举结果的那些选民。

sentences.en: For the Democrats to have the kind of night the polls say they will,
sentences.zh: 为了让民主党获得民调所预测的那种夜晚，

sentences.en: Republican-leaning voters have to decide either to stay home in enormous numbers
sentences.zh: 倾向共和党的选民必须要么决定大规模留在家中，

sentences.en: or decide to vote for Democrats in sufficient numbers in states like Kansas and Texas, Iowa, and so on,
sentences.zh: 要么决定在堪萨斯州、德克萨斯州、爱荷华州等地以足够的数量投票给民主党，

sentences.en: where in many cases they may never have voted for a Democrat for federal office before.
sentences.zh: 而在许多情况下，他们以前可能从未投票给联邦职位的民主党候选人。

sentences.en: In our polarized era, this is a tough thing to really imagine.
sentences.zh: 在我们这个两极分化的时代，这确实很难想象。

sentences.en: The consequences of a Democratic landslide or tsunami, to keep our wave metaphor going, would be really significant.
sentences.zh: 如果继续沿用我们的浪潮隐喻，民主党大胜或出现“海啸”的后果将是非常重大的。

sentences.en: It would be a repudiation of the Trump presidency right at the beginning of a presidential primary campaign.
sentences.zh: 这将是对特朗普总统任期在总统初选竞选初期的一次否定。

sentences.en: It could give Democrats control of state governments that they haven't thought of controlling in a long time.
sentences.zh: 这可能让民主党获得他们很久没想过能控制的州政府的控制权。

sentences.en: We may look back and say that it was sort of a turning point in the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 我们回过头来看，可能会说这是特朗普时代的一个转折点。

sentences.en: The beginning of the end.
sentences.zh: 终结的开始。

sentences.en: This could potentially be clearly the moment when Trump's influence on American politics began to wane,
sentences.zh: 这可能清楚地标志着特朗普对美国政治的影响力开始减弱的时刻，

sentences.en: and it was clear that he had gone too far and had broken too many promises for him to be able to preserve the coalition that had brought him and his populist politics to power.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他做得太过火了，打破了太多的承诺，以至于无法维持那个将他和他的民粹主义政治推向权力的联盟。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think we're going to leave it there.
sentences.zh: 我想我们就谈到这里。

sentences.en: I do want to give listeners, Nate, a little bit of a sense of what comes next for you.
sentences.zh: 内特，我确实想让听众对你接下来的工作有个了解。

sentences.en: You're going to walk out of here.
sentences.zh: 你待会儿就要走出这里。

sentences.en: You're going to head into these screen-filled rooms that are loaded with soda and candy to sustain you and your colleagues
sentences.zh: 你要走进那些堆满了苏打水和糖果的屏幕房，用它们来支撑你和你的同事，

sentences.en: as you count the votes and you feed them into these models and these prediction needles that we produce throughout election night.
sentences.zh: 当你们统计选票并将其输入我们在选举之夜制作的这些模型和预测指针中时。

sentences.en: And that will consume you for the next 20-something hours until you return to us at, I hope, 2, 2.30, 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 接下来的20多个小时你们都将为此忙碌，直到我希望在凌晨2点、2点半或3点回到我们这里。

sentences.en: That's what it's been in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 过去一直都是这样。

sentences.en: Wednesday morning to record our next episode because this is the first of a series.
sentences.zh: 周三早上录制我们的下一集，因为这是系列节目中的第一集。

sentences.en: And I don't know how you do it, and I'm extremely grateful to you for doing it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是怎么做到的，我非常感谢你的付出。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: For a limited time, The New York Times is making all of our election coverage free in The New York Times app.
sentences.zh: 在有限的时间内，《纽约时报》在《纽约时报》应用程序上免费提供我们所有的选举报道。

sentences.en: There, you'll find in-depth analysis, poll trackers, and live updates throughout the midterms, including on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 在那里，你可以找到深入的分析、民调追踪器以及整个中期选举期间的实时更新，包括选举日当天。

sentences.en: Plus, if it's your first time downloading the NYT app, you can access all of our journalism free for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 此外，如果你是第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序，你可以免费访问我们所有的报道30天。

sentences.en: So, give it a try.
sentences.zh: 所以，试一试吧。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth into this,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，每天晚上，你都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏品去上班，然后把DJ台变成一个，

sentences.en: like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 就像是一个充满美丽的50年历史文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼表出品的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘温娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏之一《Connections》，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: As you know, this is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，这是中期选举前的最后一天，我相信这是我们一生中最重要的一次中期选举。

sentences.en: On the final full day of campaigning across the U.S., President Trump tried to rally Republicans with a speech in front of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool,
sentences.zh: 在美国全国竞选活动的最后一天，特朗普总统试图在林肯纪念堂倒影池前发表演讲来团结共和党人，

sentences.en: where he denounced this year's Democratic candidates as extreme.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中谴责今年的民主党候选人是极端分子。

sentences.en: The Democrat Party has nominated the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history.
sentences.zh: 民主党提名的候选人名单是美国历史上最极端、最危险的。

sentences.en: These are the most dangerous candidates ever put up.
sentences.zh: 这些是有史以来最危险的候选人。

sentences.en: But many of those Democratic candidates reminded voters that Tuesday's election was, in their telling, a referendum on Trump.
sentences.zh: 但许多民主党候选人提醒选民，用他们的话说，周二的选举是对特朗普的一次公投。

sentences.en: In Michigan, the Democratic candidate for Senate, Abdul El-Sayed, mocked Trump for his repeated efforts to portray him as a radical.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州，民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德嘲讽特朗普反复试图将他描绘成激进分子。

sentences.en: For his part, Donald Trump can't seem to figure out what my actual name is, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，唐纳德·特朗普似乎搞不清楚我的名字到底是什么。

sentences.en: Abdul.
sentences.zh: 阿卜杜勒。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the Times reports that about 50 million Americans have already cast ballots,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，《纽约时报》报道称，约有5000万美国人已经投了票，

sentences.en: a surge of early voting that is outpacing the last midterm cycle in every major Senate battleground.
sentences.zh: 这股提前投票的热潮在每一个主要的参议院战场州都超过了上一个中期选举周期。

sentences.en: Polls will open this morning for in-person Election Day voting, starting at 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 投票站将于今天早上6点开放，进行选举日当天的现场投票。

sentences.zh: 还有埃里克·克鲁普克。
